title: Air fryer tandoori chicken
summary: Yogurt marinade, twenty minutes in the basket, char on the edges. About 40 g of protein a portion and barely any oil.

ingredients.qty: 400 g, boneless, cut into large chunks
ingredients.note: Thighs stay juicier here, but breast works if you pull it early.
Thin curd will not cling. Strain it if that is all you have.

ingredients.qty: 1 tsp kasuri methi, crushed between your palms

steps: Pat the chicken properly dry and cut shallow slashes into the thicker pieces.
Mix everything else into a thick paste in a bowl. Taste it - it should be aggressively salty and sour, because the chicken will mute it.
Coat the chicken, cover, and leave it in the fridge. Thirty minutes is the minimum; overnight is noticeably better.
Preheat the air fryer to 200C / 400F for 3 minutes.
Lay the pieces in a single layer with space between them. Crowding the basket steams the chicken instead of charring it - do two batches if you need to.
Cook 10 minutes, turn everything, then 6-10 minutes more until the edges are blackening in places and the thickest piece reads 74C / 165F.
Rest 3 minutes, then hit it with chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon.
tips: The dark patches are the point. If it comes out uniformly orange, it was crowded or the temperature was too low.
The leftover marinade in the bowl is raw - do not spoon it over the cooked chicken.
Same marinade works on paneer (12 minutes), cauliflower (15 minutes) or prawns (7 minutes).
health_notes: All the flavour comes from spice and yogurt rather than cream or butter, so this is a genuinely lean tandoori. Kashmiri chilli gives the red colour without the heat and without food dye.

source.adapted: Classic tandoori marinade, adapted for an air fryer and cut down to a tablespoon of oil.
